findings.title: \w matches non-ASCII letters in some engines
findings.summary: \w is ASCII-only in JavaScript but matches accented and CJK letters in Python, Rust and .NET.

engines.js-u: ASCII only (the u flag does not widen \w)

findings.title: \d matches non-ASCII digits in some engines
findings.summary: \d is 0-9 only in JavaScript but also matches Arabic-Indic and fullwidth digits in Python, Rust and .NET.

findings.title: \s covers different white-space characters
findings.summary: The set of characters \s matches differs between engines: U+FEFF only in JavaScript, U+001C only in Python, U+0085 and U+00A0 not in every engine.

engines.js: includes U+00A0, U+FEFF, U+2003, U+2028; not U+0085
engines.python-re: includes U+001C and U+0085; not U+FEFF
engines.rust-regex: Unicode White_Space: includes U+0085, not U+FEFF or U+001C
engines.dotnet: includes U+0085, U+00A0; not U+FEFF or U+001C

findings.title: \b word boundary differs next to accented letters
findings.summary: Because \w differs, \b finds a boundary between "f" and "é" in JavaScript but not in Python, Rust or .NET.
findings.rewrite: (?![A-Za-z0-9_]) or (?<![A-Za-z0-9_]) where lookarounds are allowed; otherwise avoid \b on non-ASCII text

findings.title: $ matches before a final newline in Python and .NET
findings.summary: A pattern ending in $ accepts "abc\n" in Python and .NET but rejects it in JavaScript and Rust, so a trailing newline passes on some servers only.
findings.rewrite: Reject newlines explicitly with a leading (?![\s\S]*\n) where lookahead is allowed, or validate the trimmed value

findings.title: \Z and \z are not portable
findings.summary: \Z and \z are anchors in some engines, an identity escape in JavaScript, and an error in js-u and (for \Z) Rust.

engines.js: identity escape: matches the letter Z or z
engines.python-re: \Z is absolute end; \z accepted only from Python 3.14 (error before)
engines.rust-regex: \z is end of input; \Z is an error
engines.dotnet: \Z end or before final \n; \z absolute end

findings.title: \A is not portable
findings.summary: \A is the start of input in Python, Rust and .NET, an error in js-u, and only the letter A in plain JavaScript.

engines.js: identity escape: matches the letter A

findings.title: Lookbehind support and width rules differ
findings.summary: Rust has no lookbehind; Python needs fixed width; JavaScript and .NET accept variable width.

findings.title: Lookahead is rejected by Rust regex
findings.summary: Lookahead (?=...) and (?!...) work everywhere except Pydantic's default Rust engine, which refuses the pattern.
findings.rewrite: Express the rule with several simpler patterns, or use Pydantic regex_engine="python-re"

findings.title: Backreferences are rejected by Rust regex
findings.summary: \1 works everywhere except Pydantic's default Rust engine.

findings.title: Named group syntax differs
findings.summary: (?P<n>...) is Python and Rust (also (?<n>...) in Rust); (?<n>...) is JavaScript and .NET; (?P=n) and \k<n> backreferences are not shared.
findings.rewrite: Use a plain capturing group (...) when the name is not needed

findings.title: Possessive quantifiers and atomic groups are not portable
findings.summary: a++ is accepted by Python 3.11+ and (as a plain repeat) Rust, but not by JavaScript or .NET; (?>...) is accepted by Python 3.11+ and .NET only.

engines.rust-regex: a++ accepted (as a nested repeat, not possessive); (?>...) error

findings.title: Inline flags are not portable
findings.summary: (?i) at the start is an error in JavaScript; in the middle it is also an error in Python 3.11+.
findings.rewrite: Spell out both cases in a class, e.g. [Aa][Bb][Cc]

findings.title: . matches line terminators differently
findings.summary: . rejects \r and U+2028 in JavaScript but accepts them in Python, Rust and .NET; all reject \n.

engines.js: excludes \n \r U+2028 U+2029; U+0085 is matched
engines.js-u: excludes \n \r U+2028 U+2029; U+0085 is matched

findings.title: . and characters outside the BMP
findings.summary: "😀" is one character to . in js-u, Python and Rust but two in plain JavaScript and .NET (UTF-16 surrogate pairs), so length rules like ^.{1,10}$ differ.

findings.title: [^] is only valid in JavaScript
findings.summary: [^] means any character in JavaScript and is an error elsewhere.

findings.title: \p{L} Unicode properties are not portable
findings.summary: \p{L} works in js-u, Rust and .NET, is a literal "p{L}" in plain JavaScript, and is an error in Python re.

findings.title: {,3} quantifier is read differently
findings.summary: {,3} means 0 to 3 in Python, is literal text in JavaScript and .NET, and an error in js-u and Rust.

findings.title: Unicode escape forms differ
findings.summary: \x{...}, \U00000000 and \u{...} are each accepted by only some engines; \uXXXX is accepted by all.
findings.rewrite: the literal character, or \uXXXX (surrogate pairs for non-BMP)

findings.title: Class subtraction and intersection syntax differ
findings.summary: [a-z-[aeiou]] is .NET, [[a-z]&&[^aeiou]] is Rust, and js-u rejects both (only the v flag adds set operations, and js-u is not v).

findings.title: Case-insensitive matching of special letters differs
findings.summary: With (?i), the Kelvin sign K matches k in Python, Rust and .NET; the long s matches s in Python and Rust but not .NET; JavaScript rejects (?i).

findings.title: Shorthand class as a range endpoint
findings.summary: [\w-.] works in JavaScript and .NET but is an error in js-u, Python and Rust.

findings.title: POSIX bracket classes [[:alpha:]]
findings.summary: [[:alpha:]] is a class only in Rust; elsewhere it is an ordinary class followed by stray characters (and js-u rejects it).

engines.js: nested set read as [[:alph] then literal

findings.title: Literal { and ] are not portable
findings.summary: An unterminated {2 and a lone ] are accepted by most engines but rejected by js-u (and { by Rust).

findings.title: Unnecessary escapes are rejected by some engines
findings.summary: \@ \_ \- are identity escapes: fine in JavaScript, Python and Rust, errors in js-u (and \_ in .NET).

engines.js-u: only syntax characters may be escaped

findings.rewrite: drop the backslash (put - last in a class)
